inputs.text: Five months after a ceasefire was announced in Gaza, airstrikes are still killing civilians and the humanitarian situation remains dire. Little connects Palestinians in Gaza to their prewar lives; life has become darker and far more brutal, as if the population has been stripped of its past. “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen,” said 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five displaced in Deir al-Balah.

output.main_topic: Ongoing violence and dire humanitarian conditions in Gaza after a ceasefire announcement
subtopics: Continued gunfire, shelling, drone activity, and firing at fishermen
Displacement and loss of prewar life

central_relations.object: “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen,”

output.narrative_frame: A ceasefire has not ended ongoing violence and civilian suffering in Gaza, while residents face displacement and a rupture with their prewar lives.
opinions: Life has become darker and far more brutal, as if the population has been stripped of its past.
